items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: try to get old Jesse and those guys convinced of it. Fat chance.

ctx.x: Listen, if I could have done, when I was twenty-five, twenty-six, seven years old and I was working in a saloon in Chicago, six nights a week for five years and I said I’m buried, I’m forgotten, they’ll never know who I am, help, help, I’m drowning. And I would have gladly given a toe or allowed myself to be horsewhipped to go on the road, you know, to go places. To go to England. To go to Japan. To go here, to go there. And the opportunity didn’t really occur until I got to New York in ‘75, back to New York, and…

again next May. And Scandinavia and stuff like that. And they seem to think it’s a big deal. They have work. They use it, as I was telling you, they use it sort of, which is okay, they use it as accompaniment to store features. And in Germany they have these department stores that they are allowed to take a certain deduction, amount of their taxes, in fact they’re supposed to, to support the arts. It would be a great thing in this country but, try to get old Jesse and those guys convinced of it. Fat chance. And…
Who—when you are able to play with different people overseas, who are some of your favorite musicians to play with? Is that, that’s probably a big question? Are there certain individuals?
